a monoclonal beta-hCG antibody was produced by immunization of BALB/c mouse with hCG and fusion with NS-1 myeloma cells, and that this antibody was used to develop a hemagglutation inhibition assay for hCG, and a double-antibodies radioimmunoassays for the detection and quantification of hCG.

the development and characterization of a monoclonal anti-hCG antibody.

the development of monoclonal antibodies to human chorionic gonatotropin and the use of these antibodies for the development of sensitive and specific radioimmunoassays and immunohemaglutination assays.

the development of a monoclonal anti-hCG antibody with a high affinity constant, high specificity, and high sensitivity for the qualitative detection or quantitative determination of hcg by both RIA or HAI assay.

the PE4-MAbs recognize a unique antigenic determinant on the beta-subunit and that this determinant is not shared by other glycopeptides hormones.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a monoclonal anti-hCG antibody that has the potential to be useful in both qualitative and quantitative detection of hCG.
a monoclonal anti-hCG antibody has been produced which is specific to the beta-subunit and can be used for the detection and quantitation of hCG by RIA and HIA.

the use of a double-antibodies radioimmunoassays (DARA) for the screening of monoclonal antibodies (MAb) is an efficient method for the production of monoclonal antibody specific for hCG and other related glycoprotein hormones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dual screening approach can be a powerful tool for the isolation of high affinity monoclonal antibodies with broad application in the immunoassays of biological molecules.
dual screening procedures can be used to isolate hybridomas secreting antibodies of interest.

the dual screening procedure, which is simple and easy to perform, may be a useful approach in selecting hybridoma clones producing antibodies of high sensitivity and specificity for use in the development of immunoassays for clinical diagnosis.
